newsitem.title: USA: Oscar attendees dress up and down for the evening.
newsitem.headline: Oscar attendees dress up and down for the evening.

text.p: Hollywood stars strode down the red carpet on Monday night with all eyes fixed on what they had -- or in some cases -- didn't have on.

Unlike last year's Academy Awards, when stars chose tasteful but predominantly dull ensembles to avoid controversy, this year's fashion trend was more colourful and revealing, but with a touch of elegance.

"There's a lot of skin this year, and lots of transparency but with none of the trashy flamboyance of past years. It's a sleek and elegant look," said Edward Callaghan of Beverly Hills jeweller Harry Winston, the lender of more than $20 million of precious gems to stars attending the Oscars.

Skin-tight gowns with plunging necklines were a regular feature sported by several stars including Courtney Love, star of the Oscar-nominated film "The People vs. Larry Flynt" and Emily Watson, nominated for best actress for her role in "Breaking the Waves."

"This year's trend is about beautiful, figure-revealing, translucent, sensuous clothes, in silk-satin, jerseys or chiffon," said Fred Hayman, the fashion coordinator for the 69th Annual Academy Awards.
As usual, designer Giorgio Armani had the event sewn up, outfitting several nominees and presenters including Oscars host Billy Crystal and best supporting actor winner Cuba Gooding Jr.
Best supporting actress nominee Lauren Bacall wore a long black Armani gown, cut low in the front.

With more than a billion viewers watching, Hollywood's biggest event has turned into a major marketing moment for top designers who begin wooing stars with flowers, complimentary airplane tickets and personal stylists as soon as nominations are announced.

"It's very flattering -- about 10 designers have offered to make dresses for me. I've got handwritten notes from them and flowers ... of course who knows if they'll still be interested in me after (the Oscars)?," said Barbara Hershey, nominated for best supporting actress in "The Portrait of a Lady."

Indeed, Hershey, wearing a forest green gown, lost the race to Juliette Binoche for her performance in "The English Patient," the independently-produced epic film that scored most of the night's victories.
"I was nominated for my work in an independent film, so I decided to work with an independent designer," said Binoche, wearing a rust velvet gown with a plunging neckline and stiff pointed collar.

The designers that frequently came up were Chanel, Christian Dior, and the house of Valentino, which dressed television personality Jenny McCarthy in a show-stopping and revealing dove gray and pale pink chiffon gown with inset embroidery.
"Show us the gown you're almost wearing!" asked a reporter as McCarthy strode up the red carpet.

While conventional tuxedos dominated the menswear, a few of the male stars dressed outside the norm, including last year's Oscar-winning Kevin Spacey, who wore a black velvet knee-length jacket with a black vest and black pants designed by Armani.
Flamboyant basketball star and aspiring actor Dennis Rodman also lived up to his reputation, sporting a navy blue tuxedo and top hat, with a silk red vest and ruffled shirt.
As usual, jewels lit up the evening, thanks to Winston and other jewellers such as Van Cleef & Arpel and Martin Katz.
Among Winston's loans were a 122-carat diamond necklace, bracelet and ring totalling $2.4 million, worn by best actress nominee Brenda Blethyn.

"We had a lot of men too," said Callaghan of Winston's, noting that best supporting actor nominee James Woods took his mother to the jeweller's, which lent her $2 million in sapphires and diamonds for the evening.
"Now that's a nice son," said Callaghan.
